setup.first_start: It looks like you are starting {{productName}} for the first time and have not configured a data node.
setup.data_nodes_allow: Data nodes allow you to index and search through all the messages in your {{productName}} message database.
setup.data_node_setup: You can either implement a <dataNodeLink>{{productName}} data node</dataNodeLink> (recommended) or you can configure an <openSearchLink>OpenSearch</openSearchLink> node manually. For the manual OpenSearch configuration you need to adjust the {{productName}} configuration and restart the {{productName}} server. After the restart this page will not show up again.

data_nodes.description: {{productName}} data nodes offer a better integration with {{productName}} and simplify future updates. Once a {{productName}} data node is running and you configured the certificate authority, you can resume startup.
data_nodes.registered: These are the data nodes which are currently registered. The list is constantly updated.
data_nodes.none_found: No data nodes have been found.

waiting_for_startup.title: Configuration successful
waiting_for_startup.description: The {{productName}} server is currently starting. Depending on your setup it may take a few minutes. This page will automatically refresh once the {{productName}} server is reachable. You can always refresh manually, please be aware that this page will not be visible afterwards.

error_boundary.title: Something went wrong
error_boundary.description: An unknown error has occurred. Please have a look at the following message and the {{productName}} server log for more information.

resume_startup.confirm: Are you sure you want to resume startup without a running {{productName}} data node? This will cause the configuration to fall back to using an OpenSearch instance on localhost:9200.

restart_configuration.confirm: Are you sure you want to restart the configuration? All previous changes will be deleted.

configuration_wizard.fetch_error: There was an error fetching the {{entityName}}: {{message}}

steps.certificate_provisioning: Provision certificates for your data nodes

ca_configuration.title: Configure Certificate Authority
ca_configuration.explanation_upload_or_create: In this first step you can either upload or create a new certificate authority.
ca_configuration.explanation_provisioning: Using it we can provision your data nodes with certificates easily.

ca_create.description: Here you can quickly create a new certificate authority. All you need to do is to click on the “Create CA” button. The CA should only be used to secure your {{productName}} data nodes.

ca_upload.explanation: Here you can upload your existing CA. You need to upload a single file containing both private key (encrypted or unencrypted), the CA certificate as well as any intermediate certificates. The file can be in PEM or in PKCS#12 format. If your private key is encrypted, you also need to supply its password.
ca_upload.drop_hint: Drag CA here or click to select file
ca_upload.validation_multiple_files: Please upload only a single file.

certificate_provisioning.title: Provision certificates
certificate_provisioning.configured: Certificate authority has been configured successfully.
certificate_provisioning.ready: You can now provision certificate for your data nodes.
certificate_provisioning.data_node_required: At least one {{productName}} data node needs to run before the certificate can be provisioned.
certificate_provisioning.error: Starting certificate provisioning failed with error: {{error}}

renewal_policy.title: Configure Renewal Policy
renewal_policy.explanation_automatic: In this step you can configure if certificates which are close to expiration should be renewed automatically.
renewal_policy.explanation_manual: If you choose manual renewal, a system notification will show up when the expiration date is near, requiring you to confirm renewal.
renewal_policy.error: Renewal policy creation failed with error: {{error}}

unsecure_connection.not_secure: Your connection is not secure. Please be aware the information will be sent to the server unencrypted.
unsecure_connection.maybe_not_secure: Your connection may not be secure. Please be aware the information may be sent to the server unencrypted.

configuration_finished.title: Configuration finished
configuration_finished.skipped_provisioning: You've finished the configuration successfully. You can still <goBackButton>go back</goBackButton> to provision the certificates.
configuration_finished.provisioned: The provisioning has been successful and all data nodes are secured and reachable.
